dataset: Aqueduct 4.0 country rankings: baseline water stress
attribution: World Resources Institute, Aqueduct 4.0 country rankings (2023); CC BY 4.0. Kuzma, S., M.F.P. Bierkens, S. Lakshman, T. Luo, L. Saccoccia, E. H. Sutanudjaja, and R. Van Beek. 2023. Aqueduct 4.0: Updated decision-relevant global water risk indicators. Technical Note. Washington, DC: World Resources Institute. Available online at: doi.org/10.46830/writn.23.00061.

series.measures: Baseline water stress (WRI Aqueduct 4.0 category; baseline period 1979 to 2019)
series.sourceItem: country_baseline: indicator_name bws, weight Tot (cat and label)

notes: Licence: WRI's Open Data Commitment (https://www.wri.org/about/open-data-commitment, read 2026-11-23) says WRI has adopted the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License as its standard licence for publications and data (ruling R6). The workbook's Read Me names no licence; WRI's landing page says "Creative Commons".
Read Me cautions: the indicators cannot be measured directly and have not been validated; interbasin transfers are not modelled; compare the 2023 data with the 2019 release only with caution.

Rows: sheet country_baseline, indicator_name bws, weight Tot (the other weights are Dom, Ind, Irr, Liv and One). The figures' year is 2019, the end of the 1979-2019 baseline; WRI published Aqueduct 4.0 in 2023.
WRI's -9999 "NoData" rows are kept as WRI wrote them; the map shows them as no figure.
No country row has cat -1 ("Arid and Low Water Use") in this file; the app's scale keeps that class for basins and later releases.

Check: categories and labels seen (cat: label, rows): -9999: NoData (25); 0: Low (<10%) (59); 1: Low - Medium (10-20%) (35); 2: Medium - High (20-40%) (23); 3: High (40-80%) (22); 4: Extremely High (>80%) (25).

Hand check 2026-11-23 (a separate script parsed the workbook's XML, not the DataTool): the 189 bws Tot rows' cat and label equal data.csv, every gid_0 is the app's ISO3 code; the labels of cat 0 to 4 equal the app's ShadingScales labels exactly (Low (<10%), Low - Medium (10-20%), Medium - High (20-40%), High (40-80%), Extremely High (>80%)).
